standing: PROPOSED registry owner selection v3 (record): successor RW-S2 of law J-RW r4 (docs/implementation/m3/resume-repair-jrw/PROPOSAL-r4.md, accepted by Codex, sha256 9c53bce7185399511340b3313d55379395cd7029d375cb7006a514f859ab617f). Four line overrides on selection v2's owner.md, lines 9, 60, 74 and 76, each keeping its line whole and appending text. They record that J-RW is the operation owner that authorizes ordinary, random-kind reservation completion (REG:9, :74); that completing a strict-prefix marker in place is the reservation's own interrupted step, not an overwrite (REG:60); and that this is lawful only with the complete namespace present, because REG:76's ordering rule covers every present-marker form. The carrier (I/project-registry.v2, schemaVersion 2), the schema, the physical placement, the reference model, the observation table, adoption, move, retirement and abandonment are unchanged. No code, public code, schema, inventory or product change. The exact frozen candidate requires actual independent review and root assent.

passageOverrides.before: This owner introduces private registry encoding and internal observation kinds only. It adds no public command, wire field, semantic identity input, signature domain, role state or public error code. Existing operation owners must supply authorization for installation, first-write, explicit recovery, move, fork, adoption and retirement. Their absence is not permission to invent a CLI surface or initialize on an ordinary read.
passageOverrides.after: This owner introduces private registry encoding and internal observation kinds only. Their absence is not permission to invent a CLI surface or initialize on an ordinary read. (v3, J-RW RW-S2) For ordinary, allocationKind=random reservation completion, that operation owner is law J-RW, M3's resume/repair writer (`docs/implementation/m3/resume-repair-jrw/PROPOSAL-r4.md`, item 2). Its authorization is the write gate's ordinary write admission for a durable request on the same root, whose recorded locator and incarnation agree with the row: the authorization class, on the same root, that created the reservation. It adds no CLI surface. Adoption, move, fork, retirement and abandonment keep their own owners, unchanged.

passageOverrides.before: Then, under the same fence: (1) durably publish RESERVED; (2) durably publish the new namespace directory with stable writer/readers lease inodes through the explicit initial-namespace publication profile below; (3) create-new the exact project marker, make the file and parent durable; (4) durably replace RESERVED by ACTIVE after rechecking every original root/marker/namespace observation. No project ledger, grant, Run or authoritative analysis is created before ACTIVE. Marker publication must not overwrite a tracked, foreign, different, malformed or unreadable object. Any one-sided or uncertain state ends the ordinary operation and requires explicit recovery.
passageOverrides.after: Then, under the same fence: (1) durably publish RESERVED; (2) durably publish the new namespace directory with stable writer/readers lease inodes through the explicit initial-namespace publication profile below; (3) create-new the exact project marker, make the file and parent durable; (4) durably replace RESERVED by ACTIVE after rechecking every original root/marker/namespace observation. No project ledger, grant, Run or authoritative analysis is created before ACTIVE. Marker publication must not overwrite a tracked, foreign, different, malformed or unreadable object. Any one-sided or uncertain state ends the ordinary operation and requires explicit recovery. (v3, J-RW RW-S2) Completing a marker in place is not an overwrite when its bytes are a strict prefix (the empty prefix included) of the RESERVED row's own marker frame. It is the reservation's own interrupted create-new step. It writes only the missing suffix at the existing length, rewrites no existing byte, and then makes the file and parent durable. It is lawful only inside an authorized reservation completion, with the complete namespace present (below).

passageOverrides.before: Recovery is an independently authorized local operation, not the constructor's fallback. It first performs the same whole-registry/root/marker/custody admission and observes the actual recorded state under the fence. RESERVED cannot grant a project lease or data access. RESERVED and ABANDONED are unregistered for project-lease admission: attempting flock on their file names is refused as lease-on-unregistered-namespace before lock acquisition, never treated as BUSY or permission to continue. Publishing empty lock carriers is not acquiring a lease.
passageOverrides.after: Recovery is an independently authorized local operation, not the constructor's fallback. It first performs the same whole-registry/root/marker/custody admission and observes the actual recorded state under the fence. RESERVED cannot grant a project lease or data access. RESERVED and ABANDONED are unregistered for project-lease admission: attempting flock on their file names is refused as lease-on-unregistered-namespace before lock acquisition, never treated as BUSY or permission to continue. Publishing empty lock carriers is not acquiring a lease. (v3, J-RW RW-S2) For an allocationKind=random row, J-RW is that independently authorized operation. Completion runs as its own classified step inside a later, separately admitted durable write, under the installation fence. It never runs in the process that crashed, never as the constructor's fallback, and never on a read.

passageOverrides.before: Completion requires positively proved agreement of the recorded root incarnation/locator, exact marker, and the reservation's admitted complete initial namespace/stable lease footprint, with all required durability barriers reconfirmed. Missing namespace publication may be completed only under the initial-namespace profile above from positively observed absence; an occupied incomplete or foreign namespace is unavailable and cannot be adopted from its spelling. An absent marker may be created only after the same untracked/absence/root checks as the original allocation. Only then may RESERVED→ACTIVE be published. These observations are not proof that every combination is reachable by an ordinary first-use crash. The complete admitted RegistryDocument and selected RESERVED row, including its immutable allocationKind, are mandatory recovery inputs. Ordinary reservation recovery can activate only allocationKind=random. Every allocationKind=adopt completion requires a fresh admitted-adoption context for the exact reserved ProjectId and target root, EVEN when namespace and marker are both already complete. History lookup is not a replacement for this stored kind: first adoption on another machine can have no historical ProjectId row. An unknown/missing kind or mismatching mode refuses. Ordinary first-use publishes the complete namespace before creating its marker; RESERVED plus an exact marker and absent namespace is NOT its lawful crash prefix. An ordinary reservation-recovery continuation refuses that combination. It must not infer adoption authority from the marker, RESERVED row, caller flag or directory name. The random reservation is NOT convertible to adopt; that inconsistent prefix grants no completion. A separate authorized adoption must use its own fresh adopt reservation and satisfy all original collision/retirement rules; recovery cannot silently abandon or rewrite the random row to make it fit. Unreadability/incomplete namespace still refuses in either mode.

(v3, J-RW RW-S2) Ordinary reservation completion of an allocationKind=random row may also find a marker that is a strict prefix (the empty prefix included) of the row's own marker frame. It completes that marker in place, as the marker publication paragraph above states, and only when the reservation's complete initial namespace footprint is admitted present. The ordering rule above covers every present-marker form, not only the exact one: RESERVED plus a present marker of any form (exact, zero-length, a strict prefix, ACL-omitted or private) and an absent namespace is not a lawful crash prefix, and ordinary reservation completion refuses it before any effect. This changes no row of the observation table above, which classifies without writing.
